newsitem.title: CANADA: IPL Sept. crude throughput to be reduced.
newsitem.headline: IPL Sept. crude throughput to be reduced.

text.p: September crude oil throughput on IPL Energy Inc's Interprovincial Pipe Line system to the U.S. Midwest from western Canada was expected to be reduced by an average of about 141,000 barrels a day during the month, IPL documents distributed to its shippers on Friday show.

The reduction due to maintenance from the normal flow rate of about 1.5 million barrels a day surprised shippers on Friday, who now expect a much higher rate of apportionment than had been previously thought, Canadian trading sources said.
"They had put out some notice earlier about some minor maintenance," one marketer said. "Well, minor turned out to be what we would consider as fairly significant."

He said his company's staff were estimating that September apportionment -- or the amount of crude expected to flow on the system subtracted from shipper nominations -- would now be over 10 percent, up from previous estimates of zero to one percent. "We're not very happy about that," he said.
IPL spokesman Alan Roth confirmed the reduced throughput figures, which were presented to shippers at a meeting in Calgary earlier on Friday.

According to the IPL documents, throughput on Line 2, which carries mostly light, medium and synthetic crudes, would be reduced by an average of 38,368 barrels a day, with the cutbacks starting around Sept 15.
The reduction on Line 3, which ships mostly light, medium, heavy and synthetic volumes was expected to average 58,495 barrels a day, with the cuts to start on Sept 19, the figures show.
Throughput on Line 13 was expected to be cut by an average of 30,191 barrels a day, with the reductions starting Sept 3, IPL said. The line carries mostly light oil.
Line 1, the gas liquids and products line, was slated ship an average of 13,838 fewer barrels a day, with reductions starting on Sept 4.

Lines 1, 2 and 3 extend to Superior, Wisconsin from Edmonton, Alberta, where they connect with the Lakehead system. Line 13 runs to Clearbrook, Minnesota from Hardisty, Alberta, which is southeast of Edmonton.
All are key petroleum supply pipelines to the PADD II refining market. ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
